title: Detection of Question-Answer Pairs in Email Conversations
abstract: Studies sentence-level question-answer pairing in asynchronous email conversations. The method uses email-thread structure together with lexical and contextual features to identify which earlier question an answer addresses, providing direct empirical evidence for non-adjacent reply alignment in email.

title: Using Question-Answer Pairs in Extractive Summarization of Email Conversations
abstract: Integrates automatically detected question-answer pairs into extractive summaries of email conversations and evaluates their contribution to summary quality. It provides indirect empirical validation that identifying cross-message question-answer relations captures salient structure in email threads.

title: Detection of imperative and declarative question–answer pairs in email conversations
abstract: Extends email question-answer detection beyond interrogative sentences to imperative and declarative forms. The sentence-level model uses content, context, and thread-structure features and is evaluated on benchmark email corpora, making it directly relevant to replies that answer requests or propositions not syntactically marked as questions.

title: Learning to Align Question and Answer Utterances in Customer Service Conversation with Recurrent Pointer Networks
abstract: Directly models question-answer utterance alignment in multi-round customer-service conversations. A recurrent pointer network exploits conversational context and dependencies among alignments and accommodates empty as well as multiple alignments, providing empirical evidence for responses that do not map one-to-one to prior questions.

title: Matching Questions and Answers in Dialogues from Online Forums
abstract: Studies which earlier question a dialogue turn answers in online-forum conversations. The model scores candidate question-response pairs using distance, dialogue history, and mutual attention, then constructs question-answer matches; the work also introduces a manually labeled dialogue dataset containing long-distance question-answer relations.

title: Automatic Question-Answer Alignment for Japanese Diverse Local Assembly Minutes
abstract: Targets meeting transcripts in which a participant may ask several questions together and officials subsequently answer the corresponding questions one by one. A two-stage method segments question and answer material and then aligns corresponding units, explicitly addressing multiple competing prior questions rather than assuming adjacency.
venue: 2024 11th International Conference on Advanced Informatics: Concept, Theory and Application (ICAICTA)

title: Towards identifying unresolved discussions in student online forums
abstract: Empirically analyzes discussion structures in student online forums to identify unresolved discussions and unanswered questions. The work distinguishes patterns in which questions receive answers from those in which issues remain unresolved, making it relevant to explicit modeling of missing response links.

title: Multiple questions in oral proficiency interviews
abstract: Analyzes more than one hundred question/task instances in oral proficiency interviews and documents turns containing multiple questions. It distinguishes different organizations of repeated or multiple questioning and examines how these arise around repair, missing rejoinders, and problematic answers, providing empirical evidence that response scope cannot always be inferred from the immediately preceding question alone.

title: ‘But what is the reason why you know such things?’: Question and response patterns in the LADO interview
abstract: Uses conversation analysis of LADO interviews to examine question and response patterns, including turns containing directives plus multiple questions. Interviewees often orient to a more specific or recent question rather than treating the whole preceding turn uniformly, and the study also examines confirmation and repair behavior.

title: Overview of the NTCIR-16 QA Lab-PoliInfo-3 Task
abstract: Defines an evaluated Question Answer Alignment task over Japanese assembly minutes. The task extracts topical ranges and correspondences between questions and responses in collective-questioning settings where several questions and answers can occur in batches, supplying independently defined gold and formal system evaluation for alignment.
venue: Proceedings of the 16th NTCIR Conference on Evaluation of Information Access Technologies

title: Forst: A Challenge to the NTCIR-16 QA Lab-PoliInfo-3 Task
abstract: Presents a system for the NTCIR-16 Question Answer Alignment task. It segments questioner and answerer statements and maps individual questions to answers using lexical-overlap and embedding-based information, with alignment directly evaluated against the task gold standard.
venue: Proceedings of the 16th NTCIR Conference on Evaluation of Information Access Technologies

title: ditlab at the NTCIR-16 QA Lab-PoliInfo-3
abstract: Implements question-answer alignment for governmental assembly minutes by identifying related sentence or paragraph units and comparing questions with candidate answers through several matching features. The output explicitly associates earlier questions with later answers rather than merely labeling dialogue acts.
venue: Proceedings of the 16th NTCIR Conference on Evaluation of Information Access Technologies

title: AKBL at the NTCIR-16 QA Lab-PoliInfo-3 Task
abstract: Addresses Question Answer Alignment in assembly minutes where questions and answers may be presented in batches without explicit correspondence. The system segments question and answer texts into semantically coherent units and uses BM25-based scores with a Hungarian-algorithm assignment to align them.
venue: Proceedings of the 16th NTCIR Conference on Evaluation of Information Access Technologies

title: The DialogBank: dialogues with interoperable annotations
abstract: Introduces a gold-standard dialogue resource annotated according to ISO 24617-2 across several dialogue types. Its annotations include functional and feedback dependency relations that identify the discourse material on which acts such as answers, confirmations, acceptances, and disagreements depend, making target selection explicit rather than implicit in an utterance-level label.

title: ISO 24617-2: A semantically-based standard for dialogue annotation
abstract: Describes the ISO 24617-2 multidimensional dialogue-act annotation standard and its semantic representation language. Of particular relevance are functional-dependence and feedback-dependence relations, which encode what prior discourse a responsive act depends on instead of treating response type as a context-free utterance label.

title: Identifying Agreement and Disagreement in Conversational Speech: Use of Bayesian Networks to Model Pragmatic Dependencies
abstract: Separates the problem of finding conversational dependencies from that of classifying agreement or disagreement. A ranking model first identifies which utterances form the relevant adjacency/dependency pair using lexical, durational, and structural features; pragmatic dependency information is then used to classify agreement, so attachment to the response target is part of the evaluated pipeline.

title: On the Means for Clarification in Dialogue
abstract: Provides a corpus analysis of clarification requests, their forms and interpretations, and the distance between a clarification and the utterance that triggers it. The findings show that clarification dependencies need not be represented solely as an adjacent-turn relation and motivate explicit identification of the material being clarified.
venue: Second SIGdial Workshop on Discourse and Dialogue

title: Clarifying Intentions in Dialogue: A Corpus Study
abstract: Presents a corpus-based investigation of clarification requests concerning interlocutor intentions. It distinguishes problems of intention recognition from problems of intention adoption and conducts an annotation experiment on naturally occurring candidate clarification sequences, providing empirical evidence about what a clarification targets.

title: Dependency Dialogue Acts -- Annotation Scheme and Case Study
abstract: Introduces Dependency Dialogue Acts, an annotation representation designed to capture dialogue acts together with functional, discourse, and response structure in multi-party, multi-threaded conversation. Response relations explicitly point to particular prior utterances, and a unit can participate in multiple response relations, making the representation relevant to multi-target and composite reply structure.
venue: International Workshop on Spoken Dialogue Systems Technology (IWSDS 2023)

title: In Search of the Lost Arch in Dialogue: A Dependency Dialogue Acts Corpus for Multi-Party Dialogues
abstract: Introduces a densely annotated Dependency Dialogue Acts corpus spanning multi-party classroom, board-game, and online written-game conversations. The representation annotates response and discourse dependencies in addition to dialogue-act information, and the paper evaluates baseline parsers that must recover these targeted dependencies.

title: Degrees of Subjectivity and Their Repercussions in Conversation. The View from Online Interactions
abstract: Studies English Reddit conversations annotated for speech acts and functional-dependence relations connecting discourse segments to preceding material. The analysis relates informational exchanges, answers and clarification requests, and explicit agreement or disagreement to different degrees of subjectivity, providing recent empirical data with explicit response dependencies.
venue: Workshop on Structured Linguistic Data and Evaluation (SLiDE)

title: Discourse parsing for multi-party chat dialogues
abstract: Develops a discourse parser for multi-party chat that predicts discourse attachments and relation labels among elementary discourse units. Because the parser must decide which preceding discourse unit a new unit attaches to in threaded and interleaved dialogue, it provides direct computational evidence for response-antecedent selection below the whole-message level.

title: Discourse Structure and Dialogue Acts in Multiparty Dialogue: the STAC Corpus
abstract: Introduces the STAC corpus of multi-party strategic chats annotated with full SDRT discourse structures. The data contain interleaved conversational threads and explicit discourse links between elementary discourse units, supplying empirical material for evaluating non-local response attachment rather than only turn-level dialogue acts.

title: Integer Linear Programming for Discourse Parsing
abstract: Uses integer linear programming and global discourse constraints to parse conversational discourse structures. The model jointly selects discourse links among candidate elementary units and their relation labels, so evaluation penalizes incorrect attachment as well as incorrect semantic relation classification.

title: A Deep Sequential Model for Discourse Parsing on Multi-Party Dialogues
abstract: Presents a sequential discourse parser for multi-party dialogue. For each elementary discourse unit, the model decides which previous unit it should link to and which discourse relation applies, using both local representations and global dialogue information; this directly combines antecedent selection with relation labeling.

title: A Structure Self-Aware Model for Discourse Parsing on Multi-Party Dialogues
abstract: Models discourse dependency structures in multi-party conversations with an edge-centric graph neural architecture. It reasons over candidate relations between elementary discourse units and evaluates recovery of dialogue discourse structure on established benchmarks, providing an attachment mechanism reusable for proposition-level response alignment.

title: Structured Dialogue Discourse Parsing
abstract: Treats dialogue discourse parsing as structured prediction over discourse links and relation labels. It uses global tree constraints and structured decoding rather than independent relation classification, evaluating both the organization of response attachments and their relation types on conversational discourse data.

title: A simple but effective model for attachment in discourse parsing with multi-task learning for relation labeling
abstract: Uses a BERT-based pair encoder to predict discourse attachments while jointly learning discourse-relation labels. Importantly for multi-proposition response scope, the representation permits a discourse node to have multiple parents, an empirically relevant property of multiparty conversation that is lost under single-antecedent tree assumptions.

title: Improving Dialogue Discourse Parsing via Reply-to Structures of Addressee Recognition
abstract: Improves dialogue discourse parsing by jointly exploiting addressee-recognition reply-to structure. The primary task still predicts discourse links and discourse relations between conversational units, while auxiliary reply information helps distinguish candidate antecedents rather than serving as the final whole-message output.

title: D²PSG: Multi-Party Dialogue Discourse Parsing as Sequence Generation
abstract: Formulates multi-party dialogue discourse parsing as sequence generation so that discourse attachments and relation decisions are produced within one generative framework. Experiments on conversational discourse benchmarks evaluate recovery of interactions among dialogue units, including low-resource and transfer settings.
venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing

title: Modelling Structures for Situated Discourse
abstract: Analyzes SDRT discourse structures in situated multi-party dialogue from STAC, including linguistic turns and non-linguistic events. The work empirically examines preservation of individual discourse relations and higher-order structure across annotation stages, providing evidence for graph representations richer than simple nearest-turn reply chains.

title: Dialogue Discourse Parsing as Generation: A Sequence-to-Sequence LLM-based Approach
abstract: Recasts dialogue discourse parsing as text-to-text generation with large language models and evaluates the approach on STAC and Molweni. The generative formulation can represent richer discourse graphs, including directed acyclic graphs, rather than requiring every response to have a single parent.

title: Discourse Structure for the Minecraft Corpus
abstract: Adds complete situated discourse structures to the Minecraft Dialogue Corpus using SDRT, covering both linguistic contributions and relevant non-linguistic actions. The paper also evaluates discourse parsing, including attachment and relation prediction, with particular relevance to long-distance dependencies in task-oriented dialogue.

title: Hierarchical graph fusion network and a new argumentative dataset for multiparty dialogue discourse parsing
abstract: Studies discourse parsing for multiparty argumentative dialogue, where relationships must be extracted between conversational discourse units. It introduces manually annotated argumentative dialogue datasets and a hierarchical graph-fusion model that combines contextual information to predict discourse structure, providing additional empirical evidence for nonlocal target attachment.

title: Improving Dialogue Discourse Parsing through Discourse-aware Utterance Clarification
abstract: Addresses ambiguity in dialogue discourse parsing by explicitly clarifying utterances according to discourse goals before predicting discourse relations. The system is evaluated on STAC and Molweni and aims to reduce attachment errors caused by omission, idiomatic language, and ambiguous conversational context.

title: Resolving Demonstrative Anaphora in the TRAINS93 Corpus
abstract: Reports empirical annotation and analysis of third-person pronouns and demonstratives in task-oriented TRAINS93 dialogue. The study distinguishes ordinary entity reference from demonstratives whose referents are plans or larger discourse material and motivates a resolver capable of handling both kinds of antecedent.
venue: 2nd Colloquium on Discourse, Anaphora and Reference Resolution

title: Resolving Discourse Deictic Anaphora in Dialogues
abstract: Presents an algorithm for resolving discourse-deictic anaphora in spoken dialogue. It first distinguishes individual, discourse-deictic, and vague uses of pronouns and demonstratives and then resolves discourse-deictic cases against preceding discourse, with empirical evaluation on spoken-dialogue data.

title: Dialogue Acts, Synchronizing Units, and Anaphora Resolution
abstract: Reports a corpus analysis and a model of anaphora resolution in spontaneous spoken dialogue. The analysis distinguishes nominal antecedents from sentential or discourse-deictic antecedents and from vague cases with no clearly identifiable linguistic antecedent, directly motivating null or unresolved outcomes rather than forced nearest-antecedent attachment.

title: Abstract Anaphora Resolution in Danish
abstract: Studies Danish pronouns and deictic expressions that can refer either to individuals or to abstract discourse objects. An adapted resolution algorithm is evaluated on four dialogues drawn from two dialogue collections, providing empirical evidence for dialogue-level abstract antecedent selection.
venue: 1st SIGdial Workshop on Discourse and Dialogue

title: Resolving Pronominal Reference to Abstract Entities
abstract: Presents PHORA, a system for resolving pronouns whose antecedents may denote either individuals or abstract entities evoked by prior discourse. The work explicitly broadens antecedent resolution beyond noun-phrase entity coreference and evaluates resolution of abstract referents in dialogue-oriented data.

title: Annotation of Pronouns and their Antecedents: A Comparison of Two Domains
abstract: Compares annotation of personal and demonstrative pronouns in task-oriented TRAINS93 dialogues with broadcast-news data. By annotating all pronouns rather than restricting the task to nominal coreference, the study exposes discourse and abstract antecedents that entity-only annotation schemes would systematically miss.
venue: University of Rochester Computer Science Technical Report 703

title: The Reliability of Anaphoric Annotation, Reconsidered: Taking Ambiguity into Account
abstract: Revisits the reliability of antecedent annotation with a study involving many annotators and agreement measured with Krippendorff-style methodology. Crucially, annotators are allowed to record ambiguous anaphoric interpretations rather than being forced to choose exactly one antecedent, making the work relevant to explicit ambiguity handling.
venue: Workshop on Frontiers in Corpus Annotations II: Pie in the Sky

title: Identifying reference to abstract objects in dialogue
abstract: Reports annotation experiments in which annotators identify antecedents for discourse-deictic expressions as unconstrained regions of dialogue text. Annotators show convergence on the identity of abstract antecedent regions, supporting empirical span-based treatment of propositions and discourse segments instead of restricting targets to noun phrases.
venue: 10th Workshop on the Semantics and Pragmatics of Dialogue (BRANDIAL 2006)

title: Anaphoric Annotation in the ARRAU Corpus
abstract: Describes anaphoric annotation in ARRAU, which includes task-oriented dialogue among its genres. The representation explicitly permits multiple antecedents for ambiguous expressions and discourse antecedents denoting abstract entities such as events, actions, and plans, making it useful for null, ambiguity, and multi-antecedent modeling.

title: Annotating Abstract Pronominal Anaphora in the DAD Project
abstract: Presents an annotation scheme for abstract pronominal anaphora in texts and dialogues. Antecedents may be verb phrases, clauses, or larger discourse segments, and the paper reports inter-coder evaluation, providing empirical support for span-based annotation of proposition-like antecedents.

title: Resolving Discourse-Deictic Pronouns: A Two-Stage Approach to Do It
abstract: Presents a two-stage system that first detects discourse-deictic pronouns and then resolves them to verbal or clausal antecedents. The empirical evaluation separates detection from antecedent resolution and demonstrates a computational approach to proposition-like target selection beyond entity coreference.
venue: Fourth Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2015)
